Team — forwarding Veridian's redlines. High level thoughts:

- Commercial: Veridian is pushing hard on CA law. They are a strategic early customer; losing CA law could be a showstopper.
- Risk: CA choice increases our exposure to certain discovery regimes and attorney fee statutes.
- Remedies: we should insist arbitration as default for money damages but accept an injunctive-relief carveout. The trick: carveout needs to allow emergency relief in court while preserving arbitration for merits.

Proposed fallback ladder to present to Veridian (start with more favorable ask, then concede):
  1) Governing law: Delaware (our preferred). Arbitration in San Francisco (neutral forum within CA).
  2) If customer insists on CA law: accept California law but require mandatory arbitration in San Francisco for all disputes except that either party may seek temporary injunctive relief in the federal or state courts in the Northern District of California (injunctive carveout).
  3) Add a split-costs provision for expedited injunctive proceedings (each side bears own fees for injunction phase; arbitration governs remedies after).

Questions for legal: please review the draft carveout language below and flag any absolute deal-breakers. Also note whether we should push for forum selection (ND Cal federal) as the exclusive injunctive venue or leave it broader.

Draft carveout (very rough):
"Notwithstanding any agreement to arbitrate, either party may seek from any state or federal court located in the Northern District of California temporary or preliminary injunctive relief to preserve the status quo pending resolution of the dispute; the obligation to arbitrate the underlying dispute shall remain in effect and the availability of injunctive relief shall not be deemed a waiver of the right to arbitrate."

I want to present a clear, negotiable position to Veridian tomorrow. Thoughts?

Thanks,
Marcus
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Marcus — quick markups. High-level legal guidance:

1) Governing law: we can accept CA law for this customer given strategic value, but insist on specifying Northern District of California as the emergency venue and limit forum-shopping. Put a sentence making ND Cal the exclusive venue for injunctive relief (state OR federal courts sitting in ND Cal).

2) Carveout wording: your draft is close; prefer tightening to: "Notwithstanding Section X (Arbitration), the parties agree that either party may seek temporary, preliminary or permanent injunctive relief in the state or federal courts located in the Northern District of California for issues relating to (i) alleged infringement or misappropriation of intellectual property, (ii) unauthorized use or disclosure of confidential information, or (iii) actions seeking to preserve a party's assets or business operations pending arbitration. Seeking such relief shall not constitute a waiver of any party's right to arbitrate."

3) Arbitration admin: specify AAA (or JAMS) with expedited timeline for disputes under $1M; for larger disputes use standard timeline.

4) Costs & fees: push for fee-splitting for injunction proceedings (each side pays its own attorneys' fees for emergency motions) to avoid large fee exposure upfront.

Olga/Vanessa — please review and flag any remaining exposures (esp. waiver language and discovery carveouts). If we're comfortable, Marcus should send a short, plain-language proposal to Amy that commits commercially (we accept CA law + injunctive carveout) in exchange for: (a) a mutual limitation on injunctive venue to ND Cal, (b) agreement to arbitrate merits, and (c) removal of unilateral fee-shifting in the MSA.

Laura Bennett

Subject: Proposed compromise — governing law & injunctive carveout (MSA)

Amy — appreciate you sending the redlines. We discussed internally and want to propose a concise compromise that preserves Veridian's commercial comfort while protecting Redwood's operational risk. High level: we can accept California law, subject to the following dispute pathway and carveouts.

1) Governing law: California law (to address your preference).
2) Arbitration: mandatory arbitration for all disputes arising under the MSA (administered by AAA or JAMS as agreed), with the seat of arbitration in San Francisco, CA.
3) Injunctive relief carveout: Notwithstanding the foregoing, either party may seek temporary, preliminary or permanent injunctive relief in the state or federal courts located in the Northern District of California to preserve rights related to (a) alleged infringement or misappropriation of intellectual property, (b) alleged unauthorized use or disclosure of confidential information, or (c) urgent preservation of a party's assets or business operations. Seeking such relief shall not be deemed a waiver of any party's right to arbitrate the underlying dispute.
4) Costs for injunction phase: each party will bear its own attorneys' fees for emergency injunctive proceedings; the arbitrator or court may allocate fees thereafter as appropriate.

We believe this addresses Veridian's need for CA-law comfort and immediate access to injunctive relief while keeping the merits of disputes in arbitration for speed/cost predictability. I've attached a short annex with suggested language (Proposed_Dispute_Annex.docx) for your counsel's review.

If Veridian is agreeable in principle, we can update the redline and move to signatures; if you have counter-suggestions on venue or narrowness of the carveout, send them over and we'll keep working.

Best,
